thread:
incident-bot: 🚨 Pager triggered: Authentication failures for customer CypressCorp (private VPC). High error rate on token validation for requests arriving at their dedicated ingress. Auto-escalation to on-call SRE.
aj: I'm on it — paging logs now. Do we know if this is OIDC JWKS fetch failures or upstream mTLS?
maria: seeing 5xx from our VPC edge to their JWKS URL (https://auth.cypress.internal/.well-known/jwks.json). Quick grep shows repeated 401s and TLS handshake errors.
devon: confirmed: edge logs show: 
```
TLS handshake error: remote error: tls: bad certificate
GET /v1/validate-token 502 from 10.8.3.12 -> jwks=https://auth.cypress.internal/.well-known/jwks.json
```
tia: customer-eng says they rotated certs yesterday and might have missed sidecars in the ingress fleet. Customer reported a rotation but said it was scoped to public certs only.
aj: can someone run a curl from one of the VPC egress nodes to their JWKS endpoint? Need to see full TLS output.
maria: running now on node vpc-egress-12:
```
curl -v https://auth.cypress.internal/.well-known/jwks.json
* Connected to auth.cypress.internal (10.5.2.14) port 443 (#0)
* TLSv1.3 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1):
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Server hello (2):
* error:1408F10B:SSL routines:ssl3_get_record:wrong version number
* Closing connection 0
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
{
  "error": "invalid_client_certificate"
}
```
devon: 401 + tls errors = their mTLS cert chain being rejected by our client cert verification. This matches their note about rotating certs.
oncall-sre: I'll take lead — starting incident response playbook path: "vpc-customer-auth-failure". Assigning roles: responder=aj, comms=customer-eng, remediation=maria/devon. ETA 15m for first mitigation.
customer-eng: I've reached out to the customer's infra ops (Slack DM sent). They confirmed a cert rotation but say the new certs were only uploaded to the public TLS endpoint. They will re-check the ingress certs.
aj: immediate mitigation idea: temporarily bypass JWKS fetch and use the cached key bundle we store for CypressCorp (last good snapshot at 2026-10-14T22:10Z). We have a config toggle to accept cached_jwks=true for a customer route. This will allow validation for ~30m while they fix certs. Any objections?
devon: that's reasonable. Risk: if their rotation included key material changes, using cached keys could allow expired keys to pass. But customer confirmed rotation was cert, not key rotation. Proceed if customer confirms keys unchanged.
maria: steps to enable cached_jwks on their route:
```
# patch their tenant route in controlplane
curl -X PATCH https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/tenants/cypresscorp/routes/default -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' -d '{"auth": {"cached_jwks": true, "cached_jwks_ttl": 1800}}'
```
aj: applied patch, rolling restart of edge-proxy workers for that tenant initiated. Logs show config propagated.
ops-bot: deploybot: rollout started for tenant=cypresscorp route default -> 3 shards.
maria: edges are now returning 200 for validate-token tests using cached keys from snapshot. Running synthetic tests across regions.
customer-eng: customer confirmed they are rotating their ingress sidecars now. They estimate ~12 minutes to finish.
tia: while they fix, we should also add a temporary health-check override so our circuit-breaker doesn't evict the dedicated pool. Add override: circuit_breaker: ignore_auth_failures=true for tenant during incident.
devon: adding circuit-breaker override.
```
PATCH /internal/circuit-breaker/cypresscorp
{ "ignore_auth_failures": true, "expiry": "PT30M" }
```
oncall-sre: good. Monitoring: error rate dropped from 82% -> 7% after cached_jwks enabled and circuit override. Latency stable. Marking customer impact as "degraded" not outage.
aj: handoff note — I'm on-call for next 2 hours, but I'll hand to devon at 03:00Z. If anything spikes, page oncall-sre.
maria: received new logs from customer after their ingress sidecar update — their cert chain now returns OK from our egress nodes. Doing a controlled revert: remove cached_jwks and circuit override once all nodes report healthy for 5m.
devon: running revert: PATCH removing cached_jwks.
```
curl -X PATCH https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/tenants/cypresscorp/routes/default -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' -d '{"auth": {"cached_jwks": false}}'
```
ops-bot: deploybot: rollback of cached_jwks config complete for tenant=cypresscorp.
maria: validation tests show auth validations succeed against live JWKS. No 401s from egress nodes.
customer-eng: customer says they completed sidecar rotation and validated end-to-end. Thanks for the quick mitigations.
oncall-sre: incident summary draft: issue caused by incomplete cert rotation on customer side (mTLS client cert mismatch). Immediate mitigations: enabled cached JWKS validation and circuit-breaker override for 30m, rotated back once customer finished sidecar updates. Customer impact: degraded auth for ~22 minutes, no token forgery detected. Next steps: follow up with CypressCorp to confirm cert rotation checklist includes sidecars and update runbook to add a pre-rotation validation in our control plane (validate TLS handshake from egress nodes).
aj: adding runbook task: create pre-rotation check script to probe JWKS endpoint from multiple egress nodes and verify cert chain. Ticket created: INF-2314.
maria: closing on-call. Handing to devon for post-incident blameless review docs.
devon: I'll schedule a 30-min RCA sync with SRE + customer-eng + CypressCorp for 2026-11-05 15:00 UTC.
incident-bot: Incident resolved (severity=sev2, duration=00:22:00). Postmortem link: https://docs.internal/incidents/INF-2314-postmortem
aj: thx team :thumbsup:
customer-eng: thanks all — passing kudos to oncall team.
